executiveSummary: Catastrophic flash floods along the Nepal-China border remain the dominant global crisis, with at least 1,118 deaths and more than 3,900 people reported missing as roads, bridges and hydropower infrastructure were destroyed. View Article UNICEF estimates over 17,000 children require urgent assistance in affected Nepali districts, citing needs for shelter, hygiene and psychosocial support. Supporting Report In the United States, a deadly flash flood in Grand Canyon National Park killed 1-2 people, left about 15 missing or unaccounted for, and knocked out the park's only water pipeline; more than 60-80 people were evacuated/airlifted. View Article Tropical Storm Edouard made landfall near the Texas-Louisiana border, bringing heavy rain, localized flooding, power outages and continued inland threats through midweek. View Article IFRC activated anticipatory action for drought in El Salvador to protect at-risk communities facing agricultural and water stress. Supporting Report An El Niño alert underscores elevated drought, heat, and flooding risks for more than two-thirds of children across Eastern and Southern Africa. outlook72h: Nepal-China border: Continued recovery hindered by blocked access; upstream flow variability poses renewed flood/landslide risks in some corridors-exercise caution in riverine valleys. View Article Texas-Louisiana (Edouard): Repeated downpours through midweek with localized flash flooding and travel disruption possible; monitor tornado watches where issued. View Article Grand Canyon: Water restrictions and service disruptions likely to persist while damage assessments and repairs to the Bright Angel pipeline and trail infrastructure continue. Source El Salvador: Drought conditions and livelihood stress to continue; anticipate updates to anticipatory actions and localized support plans. Source
